claims.text: The initial alloy is cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
The alloy has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
The alloy has poor oxygen resistance.
A thin alumina-forming coating can be applied by atomic layer deposition.
Pack aluminisation is an alternative intervention to atomic layer deposition.
The coated alloy is intended to operate near 1000 °C in air for 50–100 hours and at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
The intervention will rapidly produce a stable, continuous Al2O3 scale on the alloy surface.
The alumina scale will act as a diffusion barrier that limits oxygen ingress during high-temperature exposure.
Limiting oxygen ingress will mitigate oxygen-induced embrittlement.
The coating will leave the alloy's bulk microstructure unchanged.
Leaving the bulk microstructure unchanged will preserve the associated mechanical properties.
The coating will markedly reduce oxygen uptake during prolonged exposure at 1000 °C relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coated alloy will retain its high-temperature yield strength relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coated alloy will retain its room-temperature ductility relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr undergoes significant high-temperature oxidation that leads to embrittlement.
The coating's effectiveness outside the stated exposure and strain-rate ranges, including cyclic thermal or mechanical loading, is unverified.
Long-term coating adhesion, cyclic durability, and coating–substrate interface effects on fatigue remain uncertain.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis specifies ALD as the intervention, whereas the intervention and experiment allow either ALD or pack aluminisation. These are materially different treatments, so the proposal does not define a single intervention.

Retention of high-temperature yield strength is a predicted outcome and part of the falsification rule, but the listed post-exposure mechanical measurements include only room-temperature tensile ductility and yield strength, not high-temperature yield strength.
